correctness.rationale: The vertex set V={2A+B:A,B among four regular tetrahedron corners, A!=B} has 12 vertices of squared norm 11 and exactly 18 truncated-tetrahedron edges of squared length 8, with adjacent inner product 7. A generic central section has one polygon corner per edge with opposite-signed normal projections. Tetrahedral and coordinate-sign symmetries reduce normal directions to 0<=z<=y<=1, partitioned by exactly four internal vertex-normal lines into six rational planar cells. Exhaustively classifying the cell interior sign patterns gives only 4,5,6 sides, two cells each. Hexagonal cell solid angles follow the exact 3-ray determinant identity, yielding q=24/pi(atan(2/S1)+atan(1/S2)); independent edge-sign separation gives mean mu=18/pi arccos(7/11), so p4=5-mu+q, p5=mu-4-2q, p6=q. Independent rational cell counts, determinant checks, high-precision evaluation give (0.21593608531264,0.52024746523894,0.26381644944842); source supplies a separate exact rational >0.518 pentagon certificate. Six cells partition the chamber, so no appeal to Monte Carlo for universality.
